newsitem.title: USA: Ceridian settles discrimination suit, sees charge.
newsitem.headline: Ceridian settles discrimination suit, sees charge.

text.p: Ceridian Corp said Wednesday it reached an out-of-court settlement of an age discrimination suit and will pay about 313 former employees a total of about $28.5 million.
Of the total, Ceridian will be responsible for $24 million and Control Data Systems Inc the remaining $4.5 million, a Ceridian spokeswoman said.
The suit had been brought by laid-off workers of Control Data Corp, which became Ceridian after the company restructured in 1992.
Ceridian estimates that the effect on its 1997 first quarter earnings will be $0.15 a share, she said.

The suit stemmed from a series of layoffs at Control Data from 1987 to 1990. During the late 1980s, the company lost in excess of $1 billion, and its number of employees fell from 60,000 in 1983 to 10,000 in 1990, after divestitures and voluntary and involuntary terminations. At one time, over 1,000 laid-off workers were involved in the suits, but settlements and decisions reduced that number.
Ceridian had denied the charges, saying age had no bearing on the downsizing decisions Control Data made in the 1980s.

Ceridian provides systems and services for human resources departments and financial transaction services for trucking and gaming companies. The company also provides consumer and retail data to the electronic media through its Arbitron division. The company reported 1996 earnings of $181.9 million on revenues of $1.5 billion.
Control Data Systems provides integration of computer systems to businesses and government.
